structuredClone is a real deep copy that keeps Date as Date, and it handles Map, Set, typed arrays, undefined values, circular references and BigInt, none of which survive the JSON round trip (Dates become strings, Map/Set become empty objects, undefined keys vanish, circular refs throw). The JSON trick is only useful when you deliberately want a JSON-safe copy; structuredClone throws a DataCloneError on functions and DOM nodes, and neither one keeps class prototypes. Action: none needed, enjoy the coffee; if you paste the line the reviewer flagged I'll say which one fits.

`docker compose up -d` creates (or recreates) the containers, networks and volumes from the compose file and starts them in the background, picking up config changes. `docker compose start` only starts containers that already exist and were stopped, so it won't create anything or apply compose file or env changes. For this repo's local dev, `docker compose up -d db redis` is the right one, and `start` is fine only for resuming after a stop. Action: nothing to change; I can run `docker compose ps` if you want to see what's currently up.

AsyncLocalStorage lets you attach context, like a request id, to the current async call chain so any code deeper in the stack can read it without passing it through every function. The overhead is small for normal request workloads but not zero and has varied by Node version, so I'd measure on our own stack rather than quote a number. It fits the gap we just found: the api tests passed (49 files, 304 tests), and the open question is the web-to-api request id link. A Deployment manages interchangeable pods: random names, no stable identity, and any pod can be replaced or scaled freely, which suits stateless apps like our api. A StatefulSet gives each pod a stable name (pod-0, pod-1), stable network identity, ordered startup and rollout, and its own persistent volume per pod through volumeClaimTemplates. Pick it when instances need identity or their own durable storage, such as databases, Kafka or other clustered stores. Action: none needed; I'm happy to check which of our workloads would fit if you're thinking of one.
